results.question: which categories got pricier to borrow in 2025 than in 2024, going by the average agreed price on borrowings that finished?
results.sql:
SELECT 
    l.category,
    AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2024-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2025-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END) AS avg_price_2024,
    AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2025-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2026-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END) AS avg_price_2025,
    AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2025-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2026-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END) - 
    AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2024-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2025-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END) AS price_difference
FROM nlq.deals d
JOIN nlq.listings_all l ON d.item_id = l.item_id
WHERE d.deal_type = 'rental'
  AND d.status = 'completed'
  AND d.requested_on::date >= '2024-07-01'
  AND d.requested_on::date < '2026-07-01'
GROUP BY l.category
HAVING AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2025-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2026-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END) > 
       AVG(CASE WHEN d.requested_on::date >= '2024-07-01' AND d.requested_on::date < '2025-07-01' THEN d.agreed_price ELSE NULL END)
ORDER BY price_difference DESC;
results.answer: The categories that got pricier to borrow in 2025 than in 2024 are sports_outdoors and textbooks. Sports outdoors saw an average price increase from $10.53 to $11.98, and textbooks increased from $8.09 to $8.40.
